newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins rise, dip later on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins rise, dip later on profit-taking.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds rose further on Tuesday on Monday's news about Russia's rating for its forthcoming Eurobond issue but dealers said they had edged down from earlier levels on profit-taking.

The three international rating agencies, IBCA, Standard & Poors and Moody's gave Russia high speculative ratings. IBCA gave Russia BB+ for long-term foreign-currency debt, S&P gave it a BB- long-term rating and Moody's assigned Russia Ba2.
"Prices have risen much in the recent days and no wonder somebody decided to take profits. But the dip was not big, just 0.1-0.2 point," one dealer said.
Dealers said it was mainly Western operators who were selling.
"It seemed profit-taking and prices have stabilised, with new levels fluctuating 0.25-0.50 both ways," Inkombank dealer Vladislav Kovalenko said.
"There is interest to buy as well as to sell at these new yield-to-maturity levels," he added.
The yield-to-maturity on the third tranche is about 11.5 percent, and on the fourth tranche about 12.7 percent.
